newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Great Eagle to spin off property unit.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Great Eagle to spin off property unit.

text.p: Hong Kong property giant Great Eagle Holdings Ltd said on Monday it would spin off its Tai Shan Properties Ltd unit, a move analysts said would help it concentrate on higher-yielding projects.
Great Eagle said on Monday it planned to raise between HK$2.31 billion and HK$2.50 billion by spinning off its commercial properties arm.
After Hong Kong and international offerings, Great Eagle will hold 73.15 percent of Tai Shan.

"After the reorganisation and combined offering, Great Eagle will focus its resources primarily on the development of and investment in residential properties and hotels," Great Eagle said in a statement.
Andy Chau, research analyst at Mansion House Securities (Far East) Ltd said the move was good for Great Eagle.
"By spinning off its commercial properties, Great Eagle can now focus its resources on higher-yielding projects such as residential apartments and hotels," he said.
These projects offer greater returns and higher growth potential, Chau said.
Through the share sales, Great Eagle "could be able to raise funds from the market and that would substantially lower its borrowing costs", he added.

Desmond Cheung, associate director of Vickers Ballas, said: "Great Eagle needs finances for its projects. The proceeds from Tai Shan's IPO would pay off about some HK$800 million in loans it borrowed from Great Eagle.
"Great Eagle can use some of the cash raised to develop other attractive projects like hotels."

After Great Eagle last month announced net profit of HK$1.06 billion for the year ended September 30, 1996, up 28.7 percent on the year, Mansion House revised up its net profit forecasts for the company, Chau said.
For 1996/97, Mansion House raised its estimate to HK$1.264 billion from HK$1.041 billion, while for 1997/98, it raised its forecast to HK$993 million against HK$920 million.
Chau said the lower figure for 1997/98 was because the company was not expected to book any exceptional items for that year.
Chau said that while the spin-off would further enhance Great Eagles' future earnings, he added that that it would be premature to give a figure.
An analyst at a European stockbrokerage said he believed Great Eagle had chosen the right time to spin off Tai Shan.

"I am not very optimistic about commercial property. I think there will be a lot of office supply and office prices are not going to increase very much, so I think maybe this is a good time for Great Eagle to spin off its office property at the upside of cycle," he said.
Some analysts said Great Eagle was likely to consider spinning off its hotels in the medium term to further concentrate on residential property development.

"The prospects of the hotel industry are quite good," Mansion House's Chau said. "By spinning off its hotel assets, Great Eagle can reduce its debt further. It would enable Great Eagle to concentrate further on its residential developments."
Analysts said Great Eagle may ultimately become a holding company, owning majority stakes in other units with commericial or hotel interests.
Great Eagle shares closed Monday HK$1.40 or 4.46 percent higher at HK$32.80 on the day.
